comment.narrative: Regional annual data Beirut Mount LebanonBMLWE 6500 m3hayear and Bekaa BWE 9000 m3hayear

10 decrease by end of project.Change in the water use during the irrigation period from April to September as Baseline Value we refer to the value provided in the report National Water Sector Strategy Volume I Executive Summary MWE 2019 page 48 where its reported that the Region annual data Beirut Mount LebanonBMLWE 6500 m3hayear and Bekaa BWE 9000 m3hayear As per the case of study the values in the same year 2019 were 1296 m3hayear site specific value calculatedMrusti. As for Skaff 5040 m3hayear for plums and apples and 6533m3hayear for table grapes.Therefore the target aims to contribute to a reduction of 10 in the Irrigation Water Amounts provided which in the case of BMLWE is 5850 m3hayear and 8100 m3hayear for BWE. And in the specific conditions of the project the objective is to reach 1166 m3hayear for Mrusti and for Skaff Apples and plums 4536m3hayear and Table grapes 5880m3hyear.Note the report is stated every 10 years therefore its difficult to find a coherent target output unless we move to our specific case of study where we will collect the data yearly.As mentioned in the National Water Sector Strategy Volume I Executive Summary MWE 2019 page 49 the strategy is to increase the Irrigation efficiency will be improved and will be upgraded from 60 to 75 20 by rehabilitating or constructing concrete or piped conveyance structures and catchment structures and by modernizing onfarm irrigation practices microirrigation. Consequently irrigation water requirement for 1 representative ha will drop from 8400 m3hayear to 6720 m3hayear based on 5040 m3hayear as a net water requirement i.e. without water losses then 5040 0.75 6720 m3hayear would be the gross water demand per ha per year when overall system efficiency will reach 75 by 2035 therefore the project is in line with the national strategy.
Regional annual data Beirut Mount LebanonBMLWE 6500 m3hayear and Bekaa BWE 9000 m3hayear Water Sector strategy MWE 2019 page 48.
